card.title: Attempt on Existence of a hexatic phase for two-dimensional Riesz gases
card.statement: ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Source-specific calculation, conditional implication or exact obstruction Result: A rotationally invariant Gibbs mixture can have zero mean orientational order while retaining long-range two-point order. As a diagnostic let theta_x=Theta+eta_x, where Theta is uniform modulo2*pi and the eta_x are iid. Then E exp(6*i*theta_x)=0, but for x distinct from y, E exp(6*i*(theta_x-theta_y))=|E exp(6*i*eta_x)|^2, which can be strictly positive. Check: The global angle cancels in the difference and independence factors the two local terms into conjugates. Taking all eta_x=0 gives two-point order1 despite the zero one-point mean. Obstruction: Consequently a vanishing rotation-averaged one-point order parameter cannot rule out the proposed phase. A proof must establish the proper bond-orientational correlations together with positional decorrelation for the actual Gibbs law, with defects and thermodynamic limits controlled.
